data.title: Kitchen Dissolving Lab
data.description: Discover what happens when everyday kitchen items meet water and how to get them back out again.

separationMethods.description: Pour the mixture through a paper filter to trap solid pieces that did not dissolve.
separationMethods.animation: liquid passes through while solid particles stay on the filter paper

separationMethods.description: Heat the liquid until the water turns to gas and floats away, leaving the solid crystals behind.
separationMethods.animation: water boils away leaving solid crystals behind

separationMethods.description: Carefully pour off the top liquid layer because it does not mix with the water below.
separationMethods.animation: top liquid layer is carefully poured off into another container

challenges.instruction: Add the cooking oil to the water and stir. Does it dissolve?
challenges.hint: Look at the beaker after you stir: is the substance still there to see, or has it spread through the liquid?

challenges.instruction: Add the sugar to the water and stir. Does it dissolve?
challenges.hint: Look at the beaker after you stir: is the substance still there to see, or has it spread through the liquid?

challenges.instruction: Add the table salt to the water and stir. Does it dissolve?
challenges.hint: Look at the beaker after you stir: is the substance still there to see, or has it spread through the liquid?

challenges.instruction: What happened to the table salt particles when it dissolved in the water?
options: They sank and turned into sand
They spread out among water molecules
They floated to the very top
challenges.hint: Look closely at the particle view. Are the tiny pieces gone forever, or are they just hiding between the water?
challenges.narration: Salt disappears in water but it's still there—that's why the ocean tastes salty!
